title: Why We Say Turn a Blind Eye
short_teaser: The phrase is often linked to Admiral Horatio Nelson, who reportedly used his blind eye to ignore a signal he did not wish to obey.
story: The phrase is often linked to Admiral Horatio Nelson, who reportedly used his blind eye to ignore a signal he did not wish to obey. Whether every detail of the story is exact, the phrase endured because the image was memorable. Language often preserves a vivid picture even when history becomes simplified. Words shape what we notice and remember. Naming an experience can make it easier to understand, share, and use. The lasting value is not merely knowing the fact. It is seeing the pattern beneath it and considering where that same pattern may already be present in ordinary life, creative work, or business.
